questions: What should happen if rows or columns is zero? Should it return an empty DataFrame with that shape, or raise an error?
Should the random values be uniformly distributed in [0,1), or could they follow another distribution (e.g., normal) scaled to [0,1)?
Is the random seed applied globally (np.random.seed) or locally (e.g., using a generator object)?
What data type (dtype) should the values in the DataFrame have? Should it be float64, or is any numeric type acceptable?
Should the function validate that rows and columns are positive integers, and if not, raise a specific error?
If seed is None, should the random state be left unseeded (system-dependent) or set to a default reproducible state?
Should the DataFrame have default integer column and row labels, or should they be explicitly set (e.g., range-based)?
Is the function expected to handle very large dimensions (e.g., memory constraints) or should it assume inputs are reasonable?
